clue.text: Be surprised by consumption of pork pie?

definitions.text: Be surprised by consumption of pork pie?

parts.words: Be surprised by consumption of pork pie?
parts.note: a pork pie is a style of flat-crowned hat, so consuming one is literally swallowing headgear, the idiom used when something you were sure of goes the other way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pork pie' looks like the British meat pastry, but a pork pie is also a brimmed hat with a flat crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said as a promise of astonishment should an unlikely event happen, so it means being surprised.

clue.text: Cut up cold food that may be demanded

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for cut is written bottom to top

parts.note: to axe is to cut
table means food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: Chop cold dishes that might be requested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AXE into EXA, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exactable can be required or insisted upon, so may be demanded.

clue.text: Leaves space for cafe

parts.note: tea is dried leaves
room means space

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a gap in favour of a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb meaning departs, but it is tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearoom is a small restaurant serving tea and light meals, a kind of cafe.

clue.text: Boy finds me lifting handbook by telephone

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means the word me is turned upwards
by telephone means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a manual is a handbook

explanation.surface: A lad discovers someone raising a guide over the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' gives EM; 'by telephone' gives MANUEL, sounding like MANUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel is a male first name, so an example of a boy.

clue.text: A number in fifties getting grief over pension

parts.note: heartbreak is overwhelming grief
a pension is a French boarding house or small hotel

explanation.surface: Someone in their fifties suffers sorrow over their retirement income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pension' looks like retirement income, but it is a European guesthouse. 'Number' is a song and 'fifties' the 1950s, not a person's age.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak Hotel was Elvis Presley's 1956 hit, a song from the fifties.

clue.text: PC expert maybe can break the ice

indicators.note: break means the letters of the ice are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A computer specialist may be able to ease social awkwardness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A techie is someone skilled with technology, for example a computer specialist.

clue.text: Come down hard on side of east London

definitions.meaning: to strike or hit something forcefully
West Ham, abbreviated ..., is a football club based in east London

explanation.walkthrough: West Ham United is a London football team; the club's name is often shortened to W Ham in tables.
explanation.definitionFit: To come down hard on something is to strike it with a heavy blow, the sense of slamming.

clue.text: Bristled, getting beaten after resistance English put in

indicators.note: put in means the letters go inside the word for beaten

parts.note: whisked means beaten, as eggs are

indicators.note: after means the English letter comes after the resistance letter

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Someone bristled at being thrashed after resisting English rule.
explanation.walkthrough: RE goes 'put in' WHISKED, between its E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiskered means having bristles or whiskers, so bristled describes the same thing.

clue.text: Old pupil a bright one nothing bypassed

indicators.note: bypassed means the letters for one and nothing are skipped over

parts.note: luminous means bright
I is the roman numeral one
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A former student, once a clever one, was overlooked entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bypassed' removes I and O from LUMINOUS to give LUMNUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a former student of a school or university.

clue.text: At conference heads are meant to back teaching community

indicators.note: heads are the first letters of the words At and conference

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

indicators.note: to back means the word for meant is written backwards here

parts.note: meant means intended or aimed

explanation.surface: Delegates at a conference are supposed to support the teaching profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' takes AC from At conference; 'are' is A, the metric unit; 'to back' turns AIMED into DEMIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and scholars, the community engaged in teaching and research.

clue.text: One worth supporting has not succeeded in capturing intelligence vessel

indicators.note: capturing means the first piece holds the second inside it
has not means the letter for succeeded is missing from the word

parts.note: a cause is something worth supporting
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded
IQ is intelligence quotient, a measure of intelligence

explanation.surface: Someone who deserves backing failed but managed to seize a spy ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has not' drops the S, the genealogists' abbreviation for succeeded. A caique is a small Turkish or Greek boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A caique is a light rowing or sailing boat of the eastern Mediterranean, an example of a vessel.

clue.text: Briefly blow over before time

parts.note: over means excessively, as too does

explanation.surface: Someone quickly puffs before the clock runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: A toot is a short blast on a horn or whistle, so a brief blow.

clue.text: Fussy idiot rewards all but the last

parts.note: nit is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: all but the last means the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: pickings are profits or rewards

explanation.surface: A pedantic fool takes nearly every prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but the last' drops the S from PICKINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitpicking means finding fault over trivial details, which is being fussy.

clue.text: Bad advice for Americans to ferment must into alcoholic drinks

indicators.note: into means the anagram is placed inside the word for drinks

parts.note: beers are alcoholic drinks

indicators.note: to ferment means the letters of must are stirred up

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to brew grape juice into booze, given to Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must' looks like a verb but is unfermented grape juice; 'to ferment' makes UMST, which goes 'into' BEERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bum steer is American slang for misleading information or poor guidance.

clue.text: News has spread about Zorro's skill

indicators.note: about means the word for spread goes around the other piece

parts.note: to splay is to spread out
word can mean news, as in sending word

explanation.surface: Reports have circulated about the masked hero's talent.
explanation.walkthrough: Zorro is the masked swordsman of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Zorro is a fictional swordsman, so his skill is fencing with a blade.

clue.text: Joyce was this girl Henry was after

indicators.note: was after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Joyce was the girl Henry pursued.
explanation.walkthrough: Joyce looks like a woman's name, but it is the Dublin novelist James Joyce.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce was born in Dublin, so his nationality was Irish.

clue.text: New room he built for landlord?

indicators.note: built means the letters of new room he are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A new extension constructed for the property's owner.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows a landlord is only one kind of property owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord owns property, so may be a householder who owns a house.

clue.text: Goes mad with fish as unwelcome accompaniment

parts.note: flips means loses one's temper or goes mad
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone loses it when served fish they did not want.
explanation.definitionFit: The flip side is the less pleasant aspect that comes along with something, an unwanted companion feature.

clue.text: Hard-hearted guy backed old magistrate

indicators.note: backed means the whole result is read in reverse
hearted means the hard letter sits in the heart of the rope word

parts.note: a guy is a rope used to secure a tent
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A callous man supported a former judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearted' puts H in ROPE to make ROHPE, which 'backed' turns around. An ephor was one of five magistrates in ancient Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: The ephors were elected magistrates of ancient Sparta, so an ephor is an old magistrate.

clue.text: Under pressure to broadcast wrong match

indicators.note: under in a down clue means the following letters come below the letter for pressure

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to air is to broadcast
off means bad or wrong, as food goes off

explanation.surface: Under pressure to televise a fixture that went badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pair off is to match people or things into twos.

clue.text: Metal a duke concealed in cloak

indicators.note: concealed in means these letters are hidden inside the word for cloak

parts.note: a pallium is a cloak or mantle worn in ancient Greece and Rome

explanation.surface: A nobleman hid some metal in his cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Palladium is a rare silvery-white element, one of the platinum group of metals.

clue.text: Detailed fashionable sort of charge

parts.note: in means fashionable
a depth charge is an anti-submarine bomb

explanation.surface: A thorough account of a trendy type of fee.
explanation.definitionFit: In-depth means comprehensive and thorough, so detailed.

clue.text: Run over girl in African state

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the run letter sits above the girl's name

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
Wanda is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A car knocks down a young woman in an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a landlocked country in east-central Africa.

clue.text: Just look in on the High Street?

definitions.text: Just look in on the High Street?

parts.words: Just look in on the High Street?
parts.note: peering into shop displays without buying, a High Street being a town's main shopping road

explanation.walkthrough: A High Street is the main shopping street of a British town.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse the displays in stores without buying anything is merely to look at goods.

clue.text: Red down covering edible plant

indicators.note: covering means the words Red down hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Red feathers lie over a plant fit to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The eddo is a tropical plant, a kind of taro, grown for its starchy edible corms.

clue.text: Composer and first couple of players meet outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for meet goes round the other piece

parts.note: to join is to meet or come together

indicators.note: first couple of means the opening two letters of players are taken

explanation.surface: A composer and two leading performers gather outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first couple of' takes two letters, not one, from players. Scott Joplin was the ragtime composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott Joplin was an American composer famous for ragtime pieces such as The Entertainer.

clue.text: Stricken alpinist in increasing panic

indicators.note: stricken means badly affected, so the letters of alpinist are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A climber in trouble falls into growing alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailspin is figuratively a state of rapidly worsening chaos or loss of control, like mounting panic.

clue.text: Dodgy moment after judge is dismissed

indicators.note: is dismissed means the letter for judge is sent away from the word

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment

explanation.surface: A suspicious moment follows the judge being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or suspect, the same as dodgy.

clue.text: Rainproof article each gets to put on outside

parts.note: all means each in sports scores, as in two all

indicators.note: outside means the word for put on goes around the article

parts.note: to wear is to put on clothes
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A waterproof item that everyone should wear outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each' means all as in a sports score of two all, a sense easily missed.
explanation.definitionFit: All-weather describes something able to withstand any conditions, such as rain, so rainproof.
